definitions.explanation: In astronomy, a star of the first magnitude — one of the brightest stars visible to the naked eye. The magnitude scale assigns lower numbers to brighter stars, so a {一等星|いっとうせい} is in the top tier of brightness. Sirius, Vega, and Betelgeuse are familiar examples.

examples.japanese: シリウスは{有名|ゆうめい}な{一等星|いっとうせい}だ。
examples.english: Sirius is a famous first-magnitude star.

examples.japanese: {都会|とかい}でも{一等星|いっとうせい}なら{肉眼|にくがん}で{見|み}える。
examples.english: Even in the city, first-magnitude stars are visible to the naked eye.

examples.japanese: {夏|なつ}の{夜空|よぞら}には{三|みっ}つの{一等星|いっとうせい}が{大|おお}きな{三角形|さんかっけい}を{描|えが}いている。
examples.english: In the summer night sky, three first-magnitude stars form a large triangle.

examples.japanese: {天体観測|てんたいかんそく}に{慣|な}れていない{人|ひと}は、まず{一等星|いっとうせい}を{見|み}つけることから{始|はじ}めるとよい。
examples.english: Those unfamiliar with stargazing should start by locating first-magnitude stars.

notes:
Composed of {一等|いっとう} (first class, first rank) and {星|せい} (star). An astronomical term classifying stars by their apparent brightness.

BACKGROUND:
The {等級|とうきゅう} (magnitude) scale originally classified visible stars into six ranks: first-magnitude stars being the brightest, sixth-magnitude stars being the faintest visible to the naked eye under dark skies. Modern astronomy uses a precise mathematical definition, but for casual skywatching the {一等星|いっとうせい} category still means 'the brightest stars in the sky.'

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {一等星|いっとうせい}を{見|み}つける: to spot a first-magnitude star
- {夏|なつ}/{冬|ふゆ}の{大三角|だいさんかく}: the Summer / Winter Triangle (each connecting three {一等星|いっとうせい})
- {肉眼|にくがん}で{見|み}える{一等星|いっとうせい}: first-magnitude stars visible to the naked eye
- {北半球|きたはんきゅう}の{一等星|いっとうせい}: first-magnitude stars of the northern hemisphere

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {二等星|にとうせい}: second-magnitude star — the next tier down in brightness
- {等級|とうきゅう}: magnitude — the general astronomical brightness scale
- {恒星|こうせい}: fixed star — a true star (as opposed to a planet)
- {天体|てんたい}: celestial body — any object in the sky, including stars, planets, and galaxies
